evidence: The spend tracker charges a validation run only after it ends, from its record's cost (web/src/llm/evals/validation.live.test.ts:145, :164), so the reserve it checks before a run starts (:126; web/src/llm/evals/validationModels.ts:416) is what holds the $12 cap. The first run's reserve, $5 (validationModels.ts:392), priced the agent loop's output as 16,000 tokens over the whole run (:353, :363), while every request of a validation run may run to VALIDATION_MAX_TOKENS, 16,000 (:74, :86): the loop sends up to MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS + 1 requests (web/src/llm/agent.ts:269), each asking for that cap (agent.ts:318). A later run's reserve was 1.5 times the dearest run so far with a $0.05 floor (validationModels.ts:412), so after cheap runs it fell far below what a run that tunes can cost, and a run whose tokens were not reported was charged that lower figure (:428). And nothing held a run to the one tuning the reserve priced: tune_pipeline starts a tuning each time it is called (web/src/llm/tools/defs/tune_pipeline.ts:74, :95), and runCase hands the loop the tools as they ship (web/src/llm/evals/validationRun.ts:271).
proposed_fix: Option (a): a 16,000-token output cap on every validation request (plan 1.1, #101); the first run's reserve at the hard bound, the loop's 13 requests and the tuning's 15 each at 16,000 out, with the 25 % margin, every count read from its constant (FIRST_RUN_WORST: MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS + 1, VALIDATION_MAX_TOKENS, TUNE_STAGES × TUNE_REQUESTS_PER_STAGE), $7.37; a later run's reserve max(the first run's, 1.5 × the dearest so far); and a second tuning in one run only if the budget left beyond the run's reserve covers one tuning at its hard bound with the margin, $3.47 (SpendTracker.tuningBudget), held at the tool list runCase hands the agent loop (TuningGate), the skip recorded in the run (tuning_budget) and its transcript.
tests: web/src/llm/evals/validationModels.test.ts (the first run's reserve, its arithmetic step by step from MAX_TOOL_ROUNDS, VALIDATION_MAX_TOKENS, TUNE_STAGES and TUNE_REQUESTS_PER_STAGE: $7.36875, rounded up to $7.37; a tuning past the first, $3.47; every paid model covered at its own price; a later run's reserve, $7.37 after cheap runs and 1.5 times the dearest after a dear one; the hard stop at $12, a run starting at $11.99 and refused at $12.01; never past $12 over a session; a run without counts charged its reserve; the budget for a second tuning)

web/src/llm/evals/validationRun.replay.test.ts (scripted runs through runCase on a dev case: one at the hard bound, 13 loop requests and 15 tuning requests each counted at its bound, costs $5.895, inside $7.37, then the next reserve is 1.5 times it and the $12 cap stops the next run; after a cheap run the next reserve is $7.37; a second tuning the budget cannot cover is skipped, recorded at its step and in the transcript, and the run finishes; one it covers runs, and a third past its share is skipped)
note: Decided by the manager on the user's delegation, 2026-10-24; option (a) confirmed by the user. The reserve is what guarantees the $12 cap, because the tracker charges a run only after it ends: no run starts while the spend so far and its reserve pass $12 (canStart, unchanged), whatever the reserve says. The first run's reserve, at Sonnet 5.5's price in MODELS ($2/M in, $10/M out): the loop, 13 × 40,000 × $2/M + 13 × 16,000 × $10/M = $1.04 + $2.08; the tuning, 15 × 12,500 × $2/M + 15 × 16,000 × $10/M = $0.375 + $2.40; together $5.895, × 1.25 = $7.36875, so $7.37 rounded up to the cent (it was $5: $3.975 × 1.25, the loop's output at 16,000 over the run). A tuning past a run's first: $2.775 × 1.25 = $3.46875, so $3.47; on the first run $12 − $7.37 = $4.63 is left beyond the reserve, which covers one. Implemented in c12f9ba (the reserve at the hard bound, later runs, the tuning budget) and aa5dd48 (the second tuning's gate, the record and the transcript). The seam for the second tuning is the tool list runCase hands the agent loop (TuningGate in evals/validationRun.ts): it sees the run's budget (RunSpec.tuningBudget, from the live runner's tracker) and the run's tuning requests answered so far (TuningTokens), and leaves tune_pipeline and RunModel as the app has them; tune_pipeline is offered unchanged. No model-visible text changed and the snapshots are unchanged; the one string the model can newly read is a skipped call's error (TUNING_SKIPPED), in a paid validation run past its budget only. Under the $12 cap a run starts only while the spend is at most $4.63, so the dearest run before it is at most $4.63 and 1.5 times it is under $7.37: every run that starts is held to $7.37, and 1.5 times the dearest shows only in the refusal once the plan stops. Left: the loop's 40,000 tokens in a request is an estimate, not a hard bound like the output (a Claude run is neither pruned nor window-checked, runPolicy.ts); a request retried after a failure is not among the 13; and NEBULA_VALIDATION_ROUNDS above 12 would outrun the reserve's 13 requests.

decision.by: the manager, on the user's delegation
decision.option: (a) a 16,000-token output cap per validation request; the reserve at the hard bound (13 × 16k), with the 25 % margin; later runs max(first-run worst, 1.5 × dearest); a second tuning only if the budget covers it
